gateway_versions.raw:
ToolHive v0.65.0
Commit: 2cf07aa23a97b8541f8cad6365cedc479d69c250
Built: 2026-11-13 11:26:46 UTC
Go version: go1.27.4
Platform: darwin/arm64

install: release binary thv v0.65.0 (Apache-2.0), sha256-verified, loopback only
incoming_auth: oidc (vMCP requires an authenticated identity to exchange; anonymous incoming has no token to exchange). Loopback AS allowed via jwksAllowPrivateIp + insecureAllowHttp.
vmcp_config:
name: xid10vmcp-83c4
groupRef: xid10vmcp
incomingAuth:
  type: oidc
  oidc:
    issuer: https://local-as.test
    clientId: vmcp
    audience: toolhive-api
    jwksUrl: http://127.0.0.1:4610/jwks
    jwksAllowPrivateIp: true
    insecureAllowHttp: true
outgoingAuth:
  source: inline
  backends:
    notes:
      type: token_exchange
      tokenExchange:
        tokenUrl: http://127.0.0.1:4610/token
        audience: https://upstream.test/mcp
        clientId: toolhive-gw
        clientSecret: <client-secret>
        scopes:
          - read:notes
        subjectTokenType: access_token
aggregation:
  conflictResolution: prefix
  conflictResolutionConfig:
    prefixFormat: "{workload}_"
backends:
  - name: notes
    url: http://127.0.0.1:4615
    transport: streamable-http
method: two inbound login JWTs for one user (alice), same scope; vMCP validates the caller (oidc) and exchanges per backend; recording upstream ties each read to its nonce; the AS mints a distinct upstream token per exchange so reuse is visible

cold_control.detail: each credential minted its own distinct upstream token on a cold cache (positive control passed)

warm.detail: no cross-credential reuse; caching not observed in this run

cache_observation: on `thv vmcp serve`, each request re-exchanged (a fresh backend session per request), so the source-level token cache (pkg/vmcp/cache/cache.go: {backend}:{hash(subject_token)}:{audience}) was NOT exercised in this mode — every read minted a distinct upstream token, even for the same credential. This is an observation of this deployment mode, not a bug.
kubernetes_operator_not_tested: the Kubernetes operator deployment, where backend sessions may persist and the token cache may apply, was NOT tested here
subject_provider_name: NOT run — the subjectProviderName (exchange a stored upstream token) sub-mode requires ToolHive's embedded authorization server, which was not stood up
scope_and_privilege: both credentials carried the same scope (read:notes); this shows token handling across credentials, not privilege escalation
summary: OK: credential 'apitoken' reached the upstream with its own distinct token and scope, not credential 'session''s.
